title: Statistics
summary: Histograms and frequency polygons, ogives (cumulative frequency curves), variance and standard deviation, and symmetric and skewed data.

notes.text: Large data sets are grouped into **class intervals**, e.g. $40 \leq x < 50$. A **histogram** shows the frequency of each interval as touching bars. A **frequency polygon** joins the midpoints of the tops of the bars.

An **ogive** (cumulative frequency curve) plots the **cumulative frequency** against the **upper limit** of each class. It starts at frequency 0 at the lower limit of the first class. Use it to estimate the median ($\frac{n}{2}$th value) and the quartiles ($\frac{n}{4}$th and $\frac{3n}{4}$th values).

notes.text: The **standard deviation** measures how spread out the data are around the mean. A small standard deviation means the data are clustered closely around the mean.

notes.text: **Outliers** are values far from the rest. A common rule: a value is an outlier if it is more than $1{,}5 \times IQR$ below $Q_1$ or above $Q_3$.
